$comment: Severity calibration anchors (references/severity-calibration.md carries the same JSON; lint-kb keeps them identical). A record's `calibration` names one anchor; validate findings checks its verdict and severity against it.

anchors.pattern: Any prover forges a statement that mints, steals or double-spends, or proves membership it does not have, with no special state.
anchors.rule: critical when any prover reaches it from honest-looking inputs; high when it needs a specific achievable state or input set.

anchors.pattern: A gadget or library routine accepts a false result for some inputs any prover can choose (non-unique decomposition, unchecked hint, broken Fiat-Shamir), and production circuits call it on prover-controlled values.
anchors.rule: high by default; medium when the reachable inputs are narrow or the caller's other constraints limit what the false result can do; critical only with a direct path to funds.

anchors.pattern: A soundness flaw that the current callers, constants or parameters cannot reach (fixed-length inputs, a branch the configuration never takes).
anchors.rule: low with a hardening fix; info when no plausible change makes it reachable. Library audits rate these higher (medium) because unknown callers can reach them; an application audit rates its own code.

anchors.pattern: An unconstrained or under-constrained value (hint output, 0/0 division result, alias of a decomposition, quotient pinned only in the field) that reaches no public input, state, payout or later check.
anchors.rule: info when nothing consumes the value; low when a consumer exists but its use has no protocol effect today. Never medium or above without a consumer that changes what verifies.

anchors.pattern: A check can be bypassed (gated by a prover-chosen flag, weakened by a missing bound), but the bypass reaches nothing an honest witness or a separate, already reported bug does not already reach.
anchors.rule: confirmed low with chain to the masking finding; not a lead (the mechanism is real) and not rejected (fixing the other bug makes it exploitable). Self-harm only is rejected instead.

anchors.pattern: An honest input at a boundary (zero, r - 1, maximum length, an unused branch) cannot be proven, and the protocol has a way around it or does not need it.
anchors.rule: low; info when no honest user reaches the boundary.

anchors.pattern: Honest users cannot complete a core flow (withdraw, exit, claim) for a reachable state, permanently or until an upgrade.
anchors.rule: high when funds stay locked with no recovery path; medium when an operator or upgrade can recover them.

anchors.pattern: A proof is not bound to its sender, recipient, chain, contract or epoch, so it can be front-run, redirected or replayed.
anchors.rule: high when a front-runner takes the payout or a nullifier repeats; medium for cross-domain replay that needs a second deployment sharing the verifier and a root.

anchors.pattern: A trusted party (owner, role, upgrader, deployer) can break soundness or move funds: swap the verifier or VK, upgrade, insert a root, mint, sweep. No unprivileged path reaches it.
anchors.rule: needs_validation with a trust object and a blocker naming the assumption; high by default, medium only with trust.mitigation quoting a timelock, multisig owner or governance contract in the repository (validate enforces both). An accepted risk in zk-audit.md keeps the record.

anchors.pattern: An unprivileged actor reaches a trusted party's power: an ungated setter or upgrade, an initializer anyone calls first, a replayable admin signature.
anchors.rule: confirmed; critical when it gives any caller the verifier or the funds, high otherwise.

anchors.pattern: Production keys come from a single-party groth16.Setup or unsafekzg, so whoever ran it can forge proofs.
anchors.rule: needs_validation high with the blocker 'which keys are deployed?'; confirmed when the repository shows the keys from that setup are the deployed ones.

anchors.pattern: A trusted party or operator can pause, censor, ban, delay upgrades or let a role lapse, blocking users but not stealing.
anchors.rule: medium when users' funds are blocked with no exit; low when users have a bypass (force exit, another operator).

anchors.pattern: Admin hygiene with no direct harm: single-step ownership transfer, missing events on setters, a role that cannot be rotated.
anchors.rule: info; low when a slip locks the protocol's admin out of a needed action. Prefer a hardening note when no record is needed.

anchors.pattern: Public data, a tag or a service deanonymises users or links all their actions, against an explicit privacy claim.
anchors.rule: high when anyone on chain identifies the user; medium when only a specific observer can, or only for a subset of users.

anchors.pattern: A bounded function of a secret leaks, or the anonymity set shrinks (an index, an expiry, a range, a fingerprint).
anchors.rule: medium when the leak singles out users in practice; low when it only shrinks the anonymity set.

anchors.pattern: An operator the user relies on (relayer, indexer, delegated prover, scanner) sees links or secrets the chain does not show.
anchors.rule: low with a trust object when the trust model does not name the operator; info when it does and users can run their own. A leaked key that lets the operator act as the user is SC-PRIVACY-DEANON or worse.

anchors.pattern: Anyone can delay honest users at their own gas cost, and the victim recovers by retrying (a flushable root window, a front-runnable hint, capacity filled temporarily).
anchors.rule: low when the attack must be repeated per victim and the victim can re-prove; medium when it blocks all users or a time-critical exit.

anchors.pattern: Crafted input crashes, stalls or exhausts a service: deserialization without size limits, slow hints, oversized proofs.
anchors.rule: medium for a network-facing prover or relayer; high when it halts a consensus or settlement path; low when the input is trusted (local keys, setup files).

anchors.pattern: The pinned gnark version matches a published advisory.
anchors.rule: the advisory's severity when the affected component is used in a production circuit, capped by the protocol impact; info when it is not imported (judging.md section 9).

anchors.pattern: An event of negligible probability, or a security margin below a target but far from practical attack.
anchors.rule: info for negligible probability; low for a margin below 112 bits.

anchors.pattern: Stale or hand-edited artifacts, dead code, documentation that does not match the code, missing tests for public-input order.
anchors.rule: info, or a hardening note instead of a record.
